assertions.evidence: @TableTest('''...''')' appears in baseRateByZoneAndWeight, dimensionalWeightOverride, surcharges, and carrierAgnosticPricing methods

assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells.
assertions.evidence: surcharges table has three separate columns: 'Fragile | Insured Value | Handling' instead of one collapsed options map

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: Only @TypeConverter present is for ShippingZone; no PackageOptions converter from Map exists

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions column shows '[20, 15, 10]', '[30, 20, 15]' etc. as lists in all tables

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
assertions.evidence: carrierAgnosticPricing table has three separate rows with individual Carrier values, not {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} syntax

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Four methods: baseRateByZoneAndWeight, dimensionalWeightOverride, surcharges, carrierAgnosticPricing

assertions.text: Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int.
Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All tables begin with 'Scenario |' as first column

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'EU standard light', 'Large dims override weight', 'Fragile and insured' describe conditions

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
assertions.evidence: 'Cost?' appears as final column header in all four @TableTest tables

assertions.text: Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: Column headers: 'Zone', 'Weight', 'Dimensions', 'Carrier', 'Cost?' use business terms, not camelCase

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotations used, appearing in correct position before method signature

assertions.text: Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
Output contains no TestNG syntax: no @DataProvider, @Test(dataProvider=...), Object[][], or TestNG imports (org.testng.*).
assertions.evidence: Imports are only org.tabletest.junit and org.junit.jupiter; no org.testng.* present
